# Occasion and audience

## What this deck is made for

- Occasion: training while building an ISMS, once the requirements have been
  read and the implementation is due
- Audience: `practitioners`
- Length: 45 minutes, with an exercise on a clause the audience brings along
- What the audience already knows: the structure of ISO/IEC 27001 and the terms
  scope, interested party and documented information

::: {.notes}
This slide is not presented. There is only this one deck for this topic. For top
management what is needed stands in the deck on ISO/IEC 27001, because guidance
on implementation leads it to no further decision.
:::

# What it is about

## The subject in one sentence

ISO/IEC 27003 answers, for the requirements of ISO/IEC 27001, the question that
always comes after reading them the first time: what is meant by that when you
are supposed to do it.

## Why it concerns the practitioners

- The requirements are written short, and shortness is not clarity
- Anyone stuck at a clause is usually stuck at its reach and not at its wording
- Without a shared measure every reach gets renegotiated, and with opinions

# The direction it is read in

## Not from front to back

- Read from the front it is the structure of ISO/IEC 27001 a second time
- Opened at the clause where it sticks, it is the explanation to exactly that
  place
- Read the requirement first, write down what you understood, and only then take
  the guidance beside it

## Why the order counts

- Anyone reading the guidance first reads it as a requirement
- Then effort arises that nobody asked for, and it is hard to take away later
- What is binding is ISO/IEC 27001:2022; this standard is not

# What it does in daily work

## Three uses

- Understanding a clause where the implementation stalls
- Tracing an existing implementation back to the clause it hangs off
- Ending an argument about the reach of a requirement, because both sides
  recognise the same text

## Tracing back is the most useful

- For everything in the ISMS there is the question which clause it hangs off
- Where the answer is missing, either something superfluous stands there or a
  requirement is unmet somewhere else
- Both are findings, and both are cheaper than a finding in an audit

# What it is not

## Three confusions

- No audit measure: an audit holds the organisation against ISO/IEC 27001, and a
  departure from guidance is not a nonconformity
- No document template: the templates of this repository sit under `templates`
  and do not come from this standard
- No substitute for the risk work: the process behind it is filled out by
  ISO/IEC 27005, and the controls stand in ISO/IEC 27002

## One point that shows while reading

- The edition of this guidance is from 2017, the edition of the requirements
  from 2022
- So the guidance is written against the previous edition of the requirements
- At which places the requirement has changed since, this deck does not say,
  because both editions would have to be read beside each other for that

# What to do or decide afterwards

## The next steps

- Name the clause your own implementation is stuck at, and open the guidance for
  that one only
- Write down, for three existing parts of the ISMS, the clause they hang off,
  and put the ones without an answer on a list
- Set a date for the place where two opinions meet, and read the guidance
  together there
- Who, by when: belongs in the discussion and not on this slide

# References

## Standard, clause and edition

- ISO/IEC 27003:2017, as a whole standard
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 4.1 to 4.4
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 5.1 to 5.3
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 6.1.1, 6.1.2, 6.1.3, 6.2
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 7.1 to 7.5
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 8.1, 8.2, 8.3
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 9.1, 9.2, 9.3
- ISO/IEC 27001:2022, 10.1, 10.2
- ISO/IEC 27005:2022 and ISO/IEC 27002:2022, each as a whole standard

No standard wording stands on these slides. No clause number of ISO/IEC 27003 is
named, and the reason stands in the chapter on that standard: a number nobody
has looked up looks checkable and is not.
